about: Release and end-of-life dates for the database engines this package reasons about, so the patch-currency check can answer offline. A run that had to reach the network to say whether a server is behind would be unusable in the places it matters most -- a CI runner without egress, an air-gapped estate -- and would make the same question answerable differently on two days. This file is the offline truth: it is versioned, diffable, and never fetched at run time. It carries the two dates a support window is made of. It deliberately does NOT carry a current patch level per cycle: that number moves every few weeks, so a bundled copy would be wrong within a month of any release, and a wrong "latest" produces either invented findings or invented confidence. `latest_patch` is therefore null in this build, and the rule that reads it reports an undetermined with a named reason rather than a pass -- "this data does not record patch levels" is a true statement, and "you are up to date" would not be. The explicit refresh is what fills it.
provenance: Compiled by hand from each vendor's own versioning policy and release announcements, in this package's OWN shape and field names. It is deliberately not a copy of any third party's table: reusing a foreign structure would import both its license and its mistakes, and would tie a correction here to a release there.
